title: Where container secrets actually leak, and the seven habits that stop it
summary: TL;DR: Environment variables are where most container secrets live, and most leaks are boring: a .env committed to git, a password printed in a log, one key shared across dev and prod. title: The Stop List for Free Inference and Free Hosts
summary:
Most teams can name the day they adopted a free inference endpoint or a free server. Almost none can name the sentence that would make them leave it. That unwritten sentence is the actual risk, and it has nothing to do with price.

title: How Content Discovery Works in Streaming Apps
summary:
Content discovery in streaming apps is a layered pipeline. Each stage filters, scores, and surfaces content differently based on rules you control. Most teams treat it like a black box. They wonder why users scroll past everything or why niche content never appears.
We built recommendation systems for entertainment apps where the discovery model had to surface content by mood, by watch history, and by what was trending in the user's region. All at once. Without one rule drowning out the others.

Sooner or later an agent that does real work hits a login screen. The CRM wants a password, the supplier portal wants a password and a 2FA code, the staging admin wants both.
The easy fix is to put the password in the prompt, or in a file the agent can read. It works on the first try, which is exactly why it ends up everywhere. Here is what that costs and a pattern that keeps the secret on your machine instead.
